prompt: We're on day 3 of planning. Our scoping doc lists 85 dev-weeks of new work, summed across three apps (client, attendant, admin) built in parallel by separate teams. Leadership wants launch at the start of Q1, which is 13 weeks away, and we keep a 2-week buffer. The team-priority column is empty and the decisions table has 17 rows with no owner. What should we do after we finish the planning boards today?

I manage 14 engineers. Leadership approved splitting into two teams under two new managers (Priya, internal promotion; Marc, external hire starting in 6 weeks). Three engineers are at flight risk and one of them wanted the manager role Priya got. Draft the sequence for announcing and executing the split.

Finance just told me our department budget drops 18% next fiscal year. Current spend: 62% salaries (22 FTE), 21% contractors (5), 11% SaaS tools, 6% travel/training. Hiring freeze is already on. Give me a plan to hit the cut.

Two departments want different CRMs: Sales wants HubSpot (already piloted with 8 reps), Support wants Zendesk Sell because it integrates with their ticketing. IT can support only one. The contract decision is due in 3 weeks and the VP of Ops asked me to recommend. How do I run this decision?

Our patient-scheduling app had a 4-hour outage this morning; about 1,200 appointments failed to sync and 40 clinics were affected. Root cause is known (expired TLS cert on the sync service). I need to send updates to clinic managers, our CEO, and the board. What do I send to whom?

Our company OKR is 'reduce churn from 4% to 2.5% monthly'. Product's OKR is 'ship 6 new features', Marketing's is 'double signups', Support's is 'cut ticket response time 30%'. Only Support's clearly ties to churn. Q2 planning starts next week. What should I propose?

We raised a Series A and can hire 9 people this year. Current team: 4 engineers, 1 designer, founders doing sales. Revenue $40k MRR, goal $150k MRR in 12 months. Engineering says they're the bottleneck; founders say sales is. How do I sequence the 9 hires?

I'm going on 3 months parental leave in 2 weeks. I own the quarterly board deck, vendor contracts renewals (4 due during leave), and I'm the approver for the team's expenses over $2k. My deputy Sam has never done the board deck. What do I set up before I leave?
